text:
maya: Heads-up — after landing the initgen/stream batching split on canary we see a regression on p99 for medium prompts (120-300 tokens). ~8-12% higher p99 compared to master :eyes:
chris: ugh. which canary? region/us-central?
maya: canary-2026-03-17-09, us-central. Baseline run vs canary attached in the perf-bot output below.
perf-bot: Canary perf summary:
```
Baseline (master): p50=18ms p95=72ms p99=145ms tokens/s=320
Canary (initgen-split): p50=20ms p95=78ms p99=159ms tokens/s=308
```
maya: The delta looks correlated with requests that hit a warm KV cache vs cold. Decode stage seems to be waiting on a different batching window and ends up using a less optimal kernel selection.
zoe: Did batching window lengths change? we moved initgen handshake to 8ms previously, now 12ms?
sumit: yeah we increased the handshake to reduce microbatch steal but maybe it's enlarging the decode batch and pushing it into a different kernel path. Kernel selector uses seq_len distribution + batch_size heuristics.
chris: can you paste the scheduler config we used on canary?
maya: config snippet:
```
batcher.handshake_window_ms = 12
batcher.phase_split = true
queue.token_budget_target = 256
kernel.selector.bias = "latency_prefill"
```
zoe: That token_budget_target looks low for medium prompts; decode often ends up in small-batch kernel with worse throughput.
sumit: Also noticed KV priming order: prefill requests prime KV, but with phase-split the decode requests are routed to a different running pool that didn't get primed, causing extra memcpy + kernel fallback.
chris: Could be two things: (1) handshake increased -> decode batches group differently -> kernel mismatch, (2) routing policy put decodes on different affinity pool with cold KV.
maya: I captured a short perf trace showing a KV memcpy step right before decode kernel selection, causing a stall ~2.4ms on p99 traces. snippet:
```
[trace] prefill: kv_lookup=0.8ms -> enqueue -> decode: kv_memcpy=2.4ms -> kernel_select -> run
```
zoe: That kv_memcpy jump is suspicious. Is it memcpy from device->device or host->device?
sumit: looks like host staging because the target GPU buffer wasn't reserved: kernel allocator fallback path. Allocation logs attached.
chris: Proposal: revert handshake_window_ms to 8 on canary and bump token_budget_target to 512 to encourage larger decode batches and keep them on the same pool. Also ensure decode routing favors same affinity as prefill when seen in same request flow.
maya: Agreed. Quick A/B: (A) rollback handshake window, (B) keep split but add affinity pin for request flows.
perf-bot: Starting A/B test: variantA=handshake=8 token_budget=512, variantB=handshake=12 token_budget=256 affinity_pin=true
deploy-bot: Canary rollout to 10% in us-central started.
zoe: Also add a telemetry flag to record when decode falls back to small-batch kernel and whether kv buffer was reserved. That will help triage. keep it simple: counters per request id.
maya: I'll add counters + small trace dump for p99. If A reduces p99 by >5% we keep it, else try affinity pin.
sumit: FYI, kernel selector team is prepping a patch to prefer kernels with lower memcpy overhead when kv_memcpy > 1ms — might help long-term.
chris: Cool. thanks everyone. Maya, can you post results in this thread when A/B finishes? :thumbsup:
maya: Will do. ETA ~2h.
